Haldiram Begins Work on Rs 10,000 Crore IPO and Targets a Late 2027 Listing
sum: Haldiram Snacks Food, one of India's leading packaged snacks and sweets manufacturers, has formally begun preparations for an initial public offering, targeting a stock market listing in late 2027. The proposed public issue could raise around Rs 10,000 crore at a valuation exceeding Rs 1 lakh crore, according to a report by The Economic Times, citing people directly aware of the development.

The company has appointed professional services firm EY to oversee the project management office, which will handle compliance management and coordination across different business functions as part of the proposed listing process, the report said.

The IPO preparations are expected to take between six and 12 months, or potentially longer, considering the company's diversified business structure. An executive familiar with the development told The Economic Times that the company had formally begun the listing process through its project management office team.

The proposed issue size, valuation and listing timeline are preliminary and could change as the preparations progress. The company has not yet filed its draft red herring prospectus with SEBI, and it has not announced a confirmed IPO opening date, price band, lot size or stock exchange listing date.

According to the report, the proposed IPO is expected to comprise a combination of a fresh issue of equity shares and an offer for sale by existing shareholders. The split between the two parts has not been disclosed.

Haldiram Snacks Food has attracted investments from several global investors, including Singapore's Temasek, UAE-based International Holding Company (IHC), Alpha Wave Global and US-based L Catterton, according to ET Now.

Temasek, Alpha Wave Global and IHC acquired stakes in the company during March and April 2025, valuing the snacks manufacturer at approximately 10 billion dollars, or around Rs 85,000 crore at the time. The three investors collectively acquired approximately 15 per cent of Haldiram Snacks Food, while the founder-promoter Agarwal family retained an 85 per cent stake at that stage.

items.t: imran khan lawyers allowed jail meeting under ihc order
sum: Legal representatives of former Prime Minister Imran Khan have been granted permission to visit him at Adiala Jail, following a ruling by the Islamabad High Court (IHC). This meeting comes after an order mandating that Imran and his wife, Bushra Bibi, be allowed a one-hour session with their attorneys within two days.

On Wednesday, Barrister Salman Safdar and Sardar Latif Khosa proceeded toward Adiala Jail from the Dahgal checkpoint to meet with Imran Khan, complying with the recent IHC verdict. The lawyers emphasized that their discussions would focus strictly on legal matters, avoiding any political topics. Safdar remarked, “We have a meeting today. Khosa sahib and I are going. We will not discuss politics.” Meanwhile, Salman Akram Raja remained at the checkpoint during this visit.

Access to Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi at Adiala Jail has been under tight control, with meetings increasingly limited over recent months. Since December 2025, authorities have restricted weekly meetings between the PTI leader and his family or legal counsel. In April 2026, Safdar held a 60-minute consultation with Imran, per an earlier IHC directive; however, Bushra Bibi was not present. Both are reportedly held in near-solitary confinement around the clock, without access to books, media, or contact with family and lawyers.

Previous legal interventions aimed at easing these restrictions include an IHC order in June 2026 to facilitate meetings for legal formalities and appeal processes, and a Supreme Court directive in August to allow weekly family visits. Imran’s sister visited him after a nine-month interval in August 2026, and another brief meeting involving Safdar and both clients occurred in November.

The authorized meeting represents a significant moment for the continuation of legal procedures involving Imran Khan. It demonstrates judicial insistence on upholding rights to legal counsel amid highly charged political circumstances. For Pakistan’s public and legal community, this development underscores the tension between security protocols within correctional facilities and fundamental legal rights, raising concerns about detainees’ treatment and access to justice.

Nvidia shares slide as CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy raises succession fears
sum: Shares of Nvidia fell more than 4 percent on Monday, even as the broader market rallied sharply, after CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with a businesswoman alleged to be a Chinese spy, raising questions about his future at the world's most valuable chipmaker.

Huang, 63, acknowledged the affair in a message to staff on Sunday and said the board was launching an investigation into whether he was targeted by a foreign intelligence agency. The board said it had "confidence in Jensen" and no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

The New York Times first reported that the woman, Alice Huang, who is not related to the CEO, was working for China's Ministry of State Security, citing people briefed on intelligence circulated within the Trump administration in the spring. China's Foreign Ministry called the allegation "slander" and a smear.

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is the controlling shareholder of Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed International, which Nvidia lists as an official cloud partner. Megaspeed has been under US investigation over whether it helped Chinese customers obtain advanced Nvidia chips subject to export controls. Reuters said it could not independently verify the intelligence allegation.

US President Donald Trump, a close ally of Huang, said the FBI was looking into the matter. "I think that he'll be in good shape," Trump said, adding that Huang told him he had no idea the woman was a spy.

Nvidia says Huang will continue to lead the company during the probe, but the pressure is mounting. Shareholders filed a proposed class action on Monday, accusing the company and Huang of concealing his ties with the woman. Leaders from both parties are demanding briefings, while Democrats called for investigations and fresh legislation to stop advanced AI chips from reaching China's military. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries urged passage of a defense bill that restricts chip sales to China.
Analysts said the bigger worry is who would take over if Huang were forced out. "Jensen is Nvidia. Nvidia is Jensen," Stacy Rasgon of Bernstein told CNBC.

Multibagger in making! Analysts see upto 185% upside potential in this NBFC; here's why
sum: Sammaan Capital shares draw fresh brokerage coverage as IHC's capital infusion, improving asset quality and lower funding costs raise hopes of a valuation re-rating.

Multibagger stock to buy: Domestic brokerage firms have shown renewed interest in Sammaan Capital Ltd, a non-banking financial company (NBFC) seen as a potential multibagger. Analysts see up to 185 per cent upside potential in the stock, as they believe the lender is poised for a re-rating following a balance-sheet clean-up.

Sammaan Capital is expected to rally sharply as the Rs 8,850 crore capital infusion by Abu Dhabi-based International Holding Company (IHC) could support improving asset quality, lower funding costs, stronger governance and expansion into retail lending, driving earnings growth and a valuation re-rating.

Sammaan Capital, formerly known as Indiabulls Housing Finance Ltd, is a mortgage-led NBFC classified in the Reserve Bank of India's upper layer. It is transitioning into a multi-product lender and is now controlled by IHC through Avenir. IHC has committed Rs 8,850 crore (about $1 billion) at Rs 139 per share.

Shares of Samman Capital rebounded nearly 3 per cent to Rs 135.50 on Monday from day's low at Rs 131.60. It commanded a market capitalization of Rs 15,700 crore. The stock is down 32 per cent from its 52-week high at Rs 192.40 hit on June 05, 2026. The stock tested its 52-week low at Rs 111.55 on October 26, 2026.

The FY26 clean-up involved exiting a Rs 14,953 crore non-core asset pool and bringing gross non-performing assets (GNPA) and net non-performing assets (NNPA) to nil, leaving an opening assets under management (AUM) base of Rs 53,160 crore.

Arihant Capital Market identified several factors supporting its investment thesis, including IHC's ability to improve the cost and availability of capital, a strengthening liability franchise and lower funding costs. It also highlighted the clean balance sheet, potential recoveries, expansion into new lending products, operating leverage following a near-term increase in operating expenses, ample capital and improved governance.

AstraZeneca Pharma India to launch Datverzo in November 2026
sum: - Drug approved for HR-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer
- Targets patients with prior endocrine and chemotherapy exposure
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

AstraZeneca Pharma India Limited announced on November 7, 2026, that it will launch Datverzo (Datopotamab Deruxtecan) in India in November 2026. The launch follows the receipt of Import and Market Permission from the Drugs Controller General of India.

The company communicated this development to BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited. This update references an earlier communication dated December 17, 2025, which intimated the receipt of permission in Form CT-20 for the drug.

Datverzo is approved for the treatment of adult patients with unresectable or metastatic hormone receptor (HR)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer. Specifically, the drug targets patients with IHC 0, IHC 1+ or IHC 2+/ISH- status who have received prior endocrine-based therapy and chemotherapy for unresectable or metastatic disease.

The regulatory clearance marks a significant step in expanding oncology treatment options in the Indian market. The drug addresses a specific subset of breast cancer patients who have exhausted prior lines of therapy.

Global tech stocks suffer bloodbath as US midterms fuel AI fears
sum: Technology shares plunged on Friday after an unnerving rout on Wall Street as fears grew that Democrats would accelerate a backlash against AI after their crushing defeat of President Donald Trump’s Republicans in the US midterms.

The Tokyo and Seoul stock markets closed out their weeks with losses of six per cent following the Nasdaq’s 5.5pc collapse on Thursday, its worst showing since April last year when Trump unveiled his wide-ranging global tariffs.

“The tech sell-off has intensified, with the pain of the brutal sell-off on Wall Street carried straight through to Asia and knocking sentiment in Europe,” said Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club.

“Big worries are colliding — the build-out of data centres looks set to slow, which risks shredding the spending spree underpinning the boom, right at the time that investors have become super nervous about returns on this massive investment,” she said.
The London, Paris and Frankfurt stock markets shed around 2pc nearing the halfway stage despite featuring few technology firms.
Elsewhere, the dollar firmed before key US jobs data on Friday, and oil prices steadied following steep declines this week.
Futures contracts pointed to a rebound on the Nasdaq later this afternoon, but further declines for the broad-based S&P 500.

IHC’s profit jumps 87% to Dh32.3 billion as international revenues more than double
sum: International Holding Company (IHC), the Abu Dhabi-listed global investment company, reported revenue of Dh100.3 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, up 33.2 per cent year-on-year, while profit after tax surged 87 per cent to Dh32.3 billion.

Gross profit increased 35.4 per cent to Dh25.3 billion, while earnings per share climbed 129.6 per cent to Dh9.70. Profit before tax reached Dh35.3 billion, up 84.2 per cent. Return on equity stood at 20.8 per cent.
The Abu Dhabi-based company has invested in some of the world’s largest AI and technology companies, including SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic and Cerebras.
It also signed acquisition and investment agreements involving Marlan Holding RSC Ltd, Pakistan’s First Women Bank Limited and India’s Adani Group, among others.
Syed Basar Shueb, CEO of IHC, said the results reflected the growing scale of the group’s operating businesses and the expansion of its international investment platform.

“With seven of our eight business segments recording revenue growth and international revenue more than doubling, these results highlight the resilience and breadth of our businesses and their growing contribution across markets,” he said.

He added that the group would remain focused on financial discipline and selective capital deployment. IHC’s investments and partnerships in artificial intelligence, space technology, energy and mining, infrastructure and financial services were helping build “Dynamic Value Networks” to unlock new sources of growth and long-term shareholder value, he said.

Avenir Investment acquires 8.69 crore shares in Sammaan Capital
sum: - Avenir Investment acquired 8,68,92,966 shares via warrant conversion
- Transaction completed within 26 weeks of open offer expiry
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

Sammaan Capital saw its promoter, Avenir Investment RSC Ltd, acquire 8,68,92,966 equity shares on October 30, 2026. The acquisition was executed through the exercise and conversion of Tranche I Warrants, increasing the promoter's direct voting shareholding to 33.32%.

The transaction was disclosed under Regulation 29(2) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011. Avenir Investment, based in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, holds the position of promoter in the target company. The allotment of shares follows a share subscription agreement dated October 2, 2025, which triggered a mandatory open offer to public shareholders.

The conversion of warrants significantly altered the composition of Avenir Investment's holding. While the total diluted capital remained constant at 41.24%, the shift from warrants to equity shares increased the immediate voting rights percentage.

The data reveals a strategic consolidation of voting power without diluting the overall economic interest. By converting Tranche I Warrants into equity, Avenir Investment reduced its warrant holdings from 26.34% to 17.56% of the pre-acquisition capital base. Simultaneously, its direct equity stake rose from 28.34% to 33.32%. This movement indicates that the promoter is locking in voting rights ahead of potential future corporate actions or regulatory thresholds, while retaining Tranche II Warrants for future flexibility. The total diluted shareholding percentage remains unchanged at 41.24%, confirming that the conversion was purely a structural change from convertible instruments to fully paid-up equity shares.

IHC to hear plea seeking meeting with IK on 5th
sum: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) will hear on November 5 the National Dialogue Committee’s petition seeking directions for jail authorities to facilitate a meeting between incarcerated former prime minister The petition argued that the denial of visitation rights violates fundamental constitutional guarantees and prison regulations.

The petition, filed under Article 199 of the Constitution, read with Section 561 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the Pakistan Prison Rules, 1978, was submitted by National Dialogue Committee (NDC) Chairman Mahmood Baqi Moulvi along with fellow committee members Imran Ismail, Barrister Muhammad Ali Khan Saif and Fawad Ahmed.

The petitioners, all former federal ministers and senior PTI leaders, contended that the jail administration had imposed an “illegal and arbitrary ban” on meetings with the imprisoned couple since their incarceration on August 5, 2023.

The petition asserted that the respondent authorities, including the Federation of Pakistan through the Ministry of Interior, the Punjab Home Department and the superintendent of Central Jail Adiala, had “viciously compromised” the fundamental rights guaranteed under Articles 9 (right to life and liberty) and 14 (inviolability of dignity) of the Constitution.

According to the petition, meetings with Imran have been banned for almost one year, with authorities imposing restrictions that violate both national laws and international covenants, including the United Nations Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners, known as the Nelson Mandela Rules.

The petitioners specifically noted that “the family has not been granted access to their imprisoned brother and his wife, hence it is but natural to become extremely worried about his health and security during custody.”
The petition invoked the Pakistan Prison Rules, 1978, specifically citing provisions that entitle every convicted prisoner to “have an interview with his friends or relatives once a fortnight.”
